observation: Fresh main declared an 8,000,000-byte total changeset budget, but ChangesetStore.stage counted only proposed write bytes. Existing-file rollback preimages were persisted as base64 snapshots without contributing to the total, so delete-heavy changesets could retain far more repository data than the declared total budget.

decision_provenance.route_basis: This is a single boundedness and resource-integrity defect with a deterministic fresh-main reproduction, direct adjacency to the existing transactional changeset contract, and a narrow fix that reuses the current budget rather than prescribing a new architecture. The four-mode contract therefore resolves to DEEP_DEVELOPMENT without forced mode rotation.

pre_fix_reproduction: On the canonical base, five existing 1,800,000-byte files were staged as delete operations. Their 9,000,000 bytes of rollback preimages were accepted and persisted even though MAX_TOTAL_BYTES is 8,000,000, because delete operations contributed zero bytes to the total counter.
change: Count every captured existing-file rollback preimage toward the same raw-byte total budget before the changeset is persisted. Proposed write after-images continue to contribute to that total as before, so the cap now bounds the combined raw bytes represented by preimage and after-image snapshots.

validation.pre_fix_reproduction: EXPECTED FAILURE reproduced: a 9,000,000-byte delete-only preimage set staged without CHANGESET_TOO_LARGE

truth_boundary: This bounds the combined raw preimage and after-image bytes admitted into a changeset. Base64 and JSON serialization add encoding overhead above the raw-byte cap, and this change does not claim filesystem crash atomicity, arbitrary I/O-failure compensation, arbitrary complex repository synthesis, or an optimal budget policy.
